subject: Preserve declaration order of help option names

agent.result:
Done. Full suite: **1944 passed, 25 skipped, 1 xfailed** — green.

## What I changed

**`src/click/core.py` — `Command.get_help_option_names`**

It built the surviving help-option names with a `set`:

```python
all_names = set(ctx.help_option_names)
for param in self.params:
    all_names.difference_update(param.opts)
    all_names.difference_update(param.secondary_opts)
return list(all_names)
```

A `set` has no order, so `help_option_names=["-h", "--help"]` came back in whatever order the hash table happened to produce — and because CPython randomizes string hashes per process, the same program could render `-h, --help` on one run and a different order on another. That list flows straight into `help_option(*help_option_names, ...)`, so it fixes `help_option.opts`, the help output, and the info dict.

The fix swaps the `set` for `dict.fromkeys`, which de-duplicates the same way but preserves insertion order, and replaces `difference_update` with per-name `pop(name, None)` so shadowed names still drop out. I also noted the change in `CHANGES.md` under 8.5.0.

Rendering still groups short flags before long ones — `join_options` stable-sorts by prefix length, which is separate, intentional behavior I left alone. Declaration order now decides everything within a group.

## The test

`tests/test_help_option_names_keep_declaration_order` in `tests/test_basic.py`, alongside the existing help-option-name tests. Five parametrized cases assert `get_help_option_names(ctx)`, `help_option.opts`, and the literal rendered help line for: short-first, long-first, a four-name list, a case where a user param shadows one name, and a duplicated name.

**Why it fails if the fix is reverted:** the assertions demand an exact list, e.g. `["-h", "-?", "--help", "--man"]` and the line `-h, -?, --help, --man`. A `set` won't reproduce a four-element order by luck. I verified this rather than assuming — I reverted `core.py` and ran the test under 30 different `PYTHONHASHSEED` values: **it failed on 30/30**, with 3–4 of the 5 cases failing each run. The rendering assertions are literal strings, not recomputed with the same sort the source uses, so the test can't pass by mirroring a bug.
